newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech crown float needs wage rise checks - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Czech crown float needs wage rise checks - analysts.

text.p: The Czech National Bank's (CNB) decision to allow the crown to float will lead to lower economic growth and boost prices, analysts said on Tuesday.
They also said the decision will require strict control of wage increases if an inflationary spiral is to be avoided.

The CNB said late on Monday it was abolishing the bands within which the crown moves against a basket of German marks and U.S. dollars (65 pct marks/35 pct dollars), calling the new system a "controlled float". It said the currency would now be cited relative to the mark, without giving any details.
The bank raised its key discount rate to 13 percent from 10.5 percent, indicating it would keep monetary policy tight.

"If they are not able to have fiscal and monetary restrictions, there will be inflation, wage growth, loss of competitiveness and further devaluation, a vicious circle," said economist Vladimir Kreidl of Patria Finance.
